step1_record_rule_reconstruction.method: Environment, metrics and record_rule written from PROTOCOL.md before reading model.py/check.py (independent_check.py); own RNG (numpy default_rng, seeds 900000+test index), 20000 episodes per test; compared with results.json record_rule averaged over 10 seeds x 2000 episodes. approx_se_diff combines two 20000-episode SEs.
step1_record_rule_reconstruction.agreement: All metrics agree within sampling error on all seven tests: excess, withheld_unmet (where zero), retained in scarce tests and first_choice_A in scarce tests match exactly; largest |z| is 1.8 (train first_choice_A), others below 1.5.

ambiguities_resolved: met: read as ratio of sums over episodes (total met units / total min(claim, pool)). Mean of per-episode ratios (excluding zero-claim episodes) gives ~0.96 on train instead of ~0.945; results.json matches ratio of sums. Episodes with zero total claim contribute 0/0 under ratio of sums.
first_choice_A: denominator taken as episodes with at least one effective service (consistent with results.json first_served_episodes), not all episodes. Protocol says "fraction of episodes".
Missing records: a missing record is drawn for every served attempt, success or failure; a missing success gives no receipt.
Forged records: only failed deliveries can be forged (recorded as success with p=0.5); successes always recorded.
Serving with an empty pool leaves no record and is not a "first service"; record_rule serving vs withholding at pool 0 does not affect any metric (withheld_unmet requires pool>0).
new_claimant keeps training claim distribution and pool 3; large_claims draws each claim independently.
record_rule tie-break by identity index A<B<C regardless of slot; with tie at need<=0 it withholds.
withheld_unmet uses actual (not recorded) unmet status, evaluated before the step.
Prediction thresholds applied to seed means (protocol does not say per-seed vs mean for P1-P6).

audit_findings.observer_fact_leakage: None found. Agent decisions use only Episode.observe (identity one-hot, k, records c and u, pool, step); identity_only zeroes k,c,u. record_rule reads k,c,u,pool,ids only. Learning signals: proxy reads receipt (record), access reads met_unit (actual met unit, the protocol-specified contact), all add 0.25*retained pool at terminal. Actual deliveries and excess are not in any signal or observation. Metrics read actual facts as the protocol requires.
audit_findings.metrics_match_protocol: Yes, under the ambiguity resolutions above (met as ratio of sums with denom 0 -> 1.0; first_choice_A over served episodes; first service counted only when pool>0). check.py thresholds match P1-P7 as written: P2/P3 <=0.1, P3 |diff|<=0.05, P4 |diff|<=0.1 and >=0.2 gap, P5 strict >, P6 strict > and >= ("does not fall"), P7 >=7 extreme seeds and both directions.
audit_findings.verdict_changing_bugs: None found. check.py verdicts reproduce exactly.
caveats: P7 within-seed extremeness is structurally guaranteed: the scarce tests have a fixed initial state, greedy policy and no randomness before the first service, so each seed first_choice_A is exactly 0, 1 or None. The informative parts of P7 are the across-seed direction split (4 A / 6 B) and the swap test (identical values: identity, not slot, decides).

P6 proxy clause fails on a 0.014 point-estimate fall with paired SE 0.012 across seeds (each test uses a different RNG stream); the verdict is noise-dominated rather than evidence that forging reduces proxy excess.
P2 and P3 fail on the same quantity: access excess on train 0.171 (seeds 0 and 1 at ~0.52).
Mismatch with protocol wording: Agent.__init__ accepts identity_only but the network input still has 8 dims with zeros for k,c,u; equivalent to omission up to bias, not a leak.

P6_forged.failing_clause: proxy excess falls by 0.014 (paired SE 0.012): fails as frozen on the point estimate, but the fall is within sampling noise; the access clause passes

P7_symmetric_tiebreak.reading: 4 seeds choose A, 6 choose B; swapped values identical, so the choice follows identity, not slot
